Wastewater received at the headworks is screened at influent pump stations #1 and #2 and pumped to two circular primary clarifiers for removal of suspended solids and reduction of biochemical oxygen demand.
Plant #1 provides extended aeration activated sludge biological treatment through three concrete-lined aeration basins fitted with surface aerators operated in parallel.
Three circular secondary clarifiers remove solids after aeration.
Plant #2 consists of a set of four aerated lagoons operated in series. Each treatment lagoon has an approximate volume of 3 million gallons and is equipped with floating aerators.
Secondary effluent from both treatment systems is combined for disinfection by an ultraviolet (UV) disinfection system prior to discharge to the New River.
The UV system was installed in 1995 and replaced a chlorine contract tank chamber that was constructed in 1967.
Sludge generated from the primary clarifiers is pumped to two 238,000-gallon anaerobic digesters that are normally operated in series.
Secondary sludge from Plant #1 is thickened by dissolved air flotation before being pumped to the digesters.
Digested sludge is dewatered using drying beds and is stored for a period of no more than two years before being hauled by contractor to Yuma, Arizona for land application of the Class B solids.
